item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Y'know how the TARDIS disguise circuit is on the fritz and that's why it's stuck looking like a police box? Well we fixed that, and also made it a boat!

Positive reaction to self-limiting anti-anachronism mechanic and for The Foundation recognizing that they have no way to know if history had been altered. Good opinion lost when they immediately conclude that they are going to form a time navy anyway.

I am pretty sure the intent was that you can't bring living people forward to a time after they died. If you try they turn into a descendant. But that passage is ambiguously worded so it sort of sounds like corpses genealogically morph. And the expungement reads like the worst sort of "I couldn't think of anything interesting, so skip it" lazy writing.

Addendum isn't completely cringey like some older entries, but I have a pretty high tolerance for lolfoundation and I could see how opinion would vary.

If this gets picked for a re-write, I think it would be cool to really run with the anti-anachronism nature and lean into the addendum. Rho-5 tries some missions, cautious at first then increasingly blatant and desperate attempts to rig history in The Foundation's favor. Only to fail every time, or succeed and find out that their actions were already part of the original time line. You would need some sort of outside-time history verifier McGuffin, but that's something we've seen in other articels and it passed suspension of disbelief. Finale is 276 being made available for recreational use with approval since it poses no chronological dangers.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, for real. All the great time travel-related content that's been made since this went up aside, it seems content to just state that a time machine boat exists.

The only interesting thing is how it's anachronism-proof to some degree, and I think it could earn its keep if that was built on: all objects, the crewmembers, and their memories are all converted into period-appropriate equivalents. So it could theoretically be used for time-travelly missions, provided your orders can be understood and executed by 1800s-era members of the Royal British Society For Fucking Around With Ye Olde Timey Magic And Shit, which would be an interesting challenge.

It's just kinda boring. It's a boat that travels through time, that's all. Also, I think the foundation's time knowledge is inconsistent (thought that might just be me being dumb), what with
"It is unknown if operation of SCP-276 can fundamentally alter history, due to the retroactive nature of time."
and also
"After taking into consideration SCP-276's ability to "fix" anachronisms and errors in time"
Not only this, but how does it define "Modern Times?"
-1 overall.

item.title: Dang
item.content:encoded:
Too bad you become a different person if you travel outside your era. Unless you're unaffected as a person if you're on the boat? Otherwise, you could go back and try to find your most admired person and/or religious figure and ask him/her questions.

I can see how this would be an issue for some people, but dang it, if I could go back in time just once with a return trip to my time, that's so what I would do.

Of course, as an SCP, the way it is just makes it harder to screw up certain times when time-traveling.
